Definition: contracted from a compound of G735 and G1435; gift of Artemis; Artemas (or Artemidorus), a Christian:--Artemas.
BiblicalUsage: Artemas is named once, as the man Paul will send to Titus in Crete, or Tychicus in his place. Paul tells Titus to be diligent to come to him at Nicopolis, where he has decided to winter, and Artemas is the one who will take over the work.
TheologicalSignificance: A man named once as a replacement tells me the work of the church goes on by handover: one man comes, another goes, and the gospel stays in Crete either way.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
